findings.F1: A coin's 24-hour return predicts the next 24 hours in reverse, and almost entirely after falls. On the non-overlapping 24-hour grid, regressing excess next-24h return on the coin-standardised past-24h return gives a slope of -0.0107 (t -13.9, n 8716) when the past return is below the coin's mean, against -0.0025 (t -3.7, n 8386) when it is above. Within those falls, the deepest quarter is followed by +0.74% excess (t 5.2, n 2179), while the other three quarters show -0.08% to -0.18%.
findings.F2: The rebound after large 24-hour falls shows in every coin and nearly every year. For the bottom fifth of past-24h returns, the next-24h excess is +0.25% to +0.61% in all six coins (t 1.4 to 2.4) and positive in all eight years 2018–2025 (t 0.3 to 2.6, with 2022 the weakest at +0.08%).
findings.F3: The rebound after falls lasts beyond one day. On falls, the slope of excess return on the past return stays negative:
findings.F4: The hours 21:00 and 22:00 UTC carry a positive 1-hour drift (mean +0.055%, t 6.9, and +0.044%, t 5.8), the largest of the 24 hours. The excess return over those two hours is positive in all six coins (t 2.6 to 4.0), in seven of eight years (2022 is the exception at t -1.9) and on every weekday (t 1.5 to 3.6). It does not grow with the past 20-hour return (slope t -1.4, n 17261).
findings.F5: The tested book loses to its own churn. Its gross gain per day is positive in BTC, ETH and XRP (+0.09% to +0.11%), but fees per day are larger in every coin (0.155% to 0.250%). Trades held 3 hours or less lose 0.54% to 0.78% before fees (about 30,700 trades), while trades held over 14 hours gain 3.47% (12,610 trades).
findings.F6: The tested forecast does better over two weeks than over a day. In the trending regime, the top half of positive forecasts is followed by +4.7% excess over the next 336 hours (t 1.9, n 181), but by -0.15% over the next 24 hours (t -1.6, n 2898). This matches the plan's slope t of 2.18 alongside a losing hourly book.

ideas.idea: The deeper a coin's fall over the past day, the larger its rise over the next one to three days.
ideas.consequence: After a sharp one-day drop, a trader has reason to buy for a rebound over the next day or so rather than sell into the move, more so the deeper the drop.
ideas.name: one-day fall rebound

ideas.idea: The deeper a coin's fall over the past week, the larger its rise over the following week.
ideas.consequence: A trader has reason to lean long, rather than short, on coins that fell hardest over the past week, holding for about a week.
ideas.name: weekly fall reversal

ideas.name: near-high momentum, daily bars
ideas.idea: When a coin closes above its long moving average, the nearer its close sits to the top of its recent range and the stronger its recent rise, the larger its return over the following days to two weeks. The effect fades by about a month.
ideas.consequence: Hold momentum longs inside an uptrend for days to a couple of weeks, not a month, and size them by how close price is to its recent high.
